content.value_statement: Developers often need a concise reminder for common implementation patterns. This skill provides compact TypeScript examples for selecting and adapting proven structures.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Factory, Builder, Singleton, Adapter, Decorator, Strategy, and Observer patterns.
Provides TypeScript examples for error handling with Result types and retry with backoff.
Shows async control examples for promise queues and debounce functions.
Summarizes repository and unit of work patterns for data access design.
Includes a comparison table that maps common engineering problems to matching patterns.
limitations: It is a static reference and does not inspect or modify project code.
Examples are simplified and require review before production use.
It focuses on TypeScript-style examples, not every programming language.
It does not provide runnable tests or complete application scaffolds.

use_cases.title: Choose a Design Pattern
use_cases.description: Compare common object creation, structure, and behavior patterns before implementing a feature.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Options
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to discuss tradeoffs during code review or technical planning.

use_cases.title: Teach Common Patterns
use_cases.description: Give learners short examples that explain when each pattern is useful.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Matching Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a simple implementation problem.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-patterns skill to suggest a pattern for this problem: [describe the problem]. Explain why it fits in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an Example
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a reference pattern into project-specific guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-patterns skill to adapt the most relevant TypeScript pattern for this feature: [feature details]. Keep the explanation practical.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Alternatives
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate two or more possible patterns before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-patterns skill to compare possible patterns for [engineering problem]. Include benefits, drawbacks, and when to avoid each one.

prompt_templates.title: Review Pattern Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing design decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-patterns skill to review whether [current approach] is the right pattern for [context]. Identify risks and a better option if needed.

output_examples.input: I need to create different payment handlers at runtime.
output_examples.output: The skill would point to the Strategy pattern. It would explain that each payment method can share one interface while the checkout flow selects the active behavior.

output_examples.input: I need to limit rapid search requests from a text box.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest the debounce pattern. It would describe waiting briefly after typing before running the search action.

output_examples.input: I need to coordinate several repository writes as one operation.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend the Unit of Work pattern. It would explain grouping writes inside one transaction boundary with rollback on failure.

best_practices: Treat each example as a starting point and adjust it to project constraints.
Choose the simplest pattern that solves the current problem clearly.
Review concurrency, transaction, and error handling examples before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not add a design pattern when a simple function or class is enough.
Do not copy examples directly without types, tests, and error handling for your project.
Do not use Singleton for shared state unless lifecycle and test impact are understood.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides a concise reference for common TypeScript code patterns and when to use them.

faq.question: Does it execute code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown reference file with illustrative examples only.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Use them as starting points. Add validation, tests, and project-specific error handling first.

faq.question: What languages does it focus on?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript-style syntax and concepts.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes safe parameterized query and transaction examples, but it is not a full security guide.
